title: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST)
subject: anaesthesia
setting: Operating theatre, labour ward, emergency department, day-care and procedure rooms
summary: Stop the injection, call for help, secure the airway with 100% oxygen, treat seizures with a benzodiazepine, give 20% lipid emulsion early (1.5 mL/kg bolus then 0.25 mL/kg/min under 70 kg), and run modified resuscitation with small adrenaline doses and no vasopressin or lidocaine.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Usually within seconds to minutes of injection, but can be delayed (up to hours with fascial plane blocks or continuous infusions, sometimes days into an infusion).
CNS: perioral numbness, metallic taste, tinnitus, lightheadedness, agitation, confusion, then seizures, reduced consciousness and apnoea.

Cardiovascular: early hypertension and tachycardia, then bradycardia, conduction block, hypotension, ventricular arrhythmias and asystole. About one in five episodes has cardiovascular signs without CNS warning.
Suspect LAST in any patient with altered mental state, seizures or cardiovascular collapse after a local anaesthetic by any route (nerve block, epidural, infiltration, tumescent, topical, IV).

sections.title: Immediate actions
items: Stop injecting. Call for help and get the LAST kit (20% lipid emulsion and checklist). Consider alerting a cardiopulmonary bypass or ECMO team early.
Airway: 100% oxygen, ventilate and intubate as needed. Avoid hypoxia, hypercapnia and acidosis, which worsen toxicity; avoid hyperventilation-induced alkalosis too.
Seizures: a benzodiazepine is preferred. If only propofol is available use small doses (for example 20 mg increments), and avoid it if there is cardiovascular instability.
Give 20% lipid emulsion early, at the first sign of serious toxicity; the order (bolus or infusion) and method of infusion are not critical.
Cardiac arrest: start CPR and advanced life support with the modifications below; resuscitation may need to continue for an hour or longer.

sections.title: Lipid emulsion and modified resuscitation
items: Over 70 kg: 20% lipid bolus about 100 mL over 2 to 3 minutes, then infuse about 200 to 250 mL over 15 to 20 minutes.
Under 70 kg: bolus 1.5 mL/kg (lean body weight) over 2 to 3 minutes, then 0.25 mL/kg/min; consider a pump if under 40 kg.
If still unstable: repeat the bolus (once or twice) and double the infusion rate. Continue the infusion for at least 15 minutes after stability returns. Maximum total about 12 mL/kg.
Adrenaline: use smaller than standard doses, starting at 1 mcg/kg or less per bolus, rather than 1 mg.
Avoid vasopressin, calcium channel blockers, beta-blockers and local anaesthetics (no lidocaine as an antiarrhythmic). Amiodarone is the preferred antiarrhythmic.
Propofol is not a substitute for lipid emulsion (too little lipid, and it depresses the myocardium).

sections.title: Monitoring and disposition
items: Once stable, observe at least 2 hours after an isolated seizure and 4 to 6 hours after cardiovascular instability; after cardiac arrest, admit to ICU.
Continuous ECG, blood pressure and SpO2; blood gas for acidosis and hypoxaemia.
After lipid, watch for pancreatitis and expect interference with some laboratory tests (lipaemic samples).
Report the event and review the dose and technique used.

sections.title: Prevention: dose and technique
items: Calculate the maximum dose before drawing up, using lean body weight in obesity; toxicity of different local anaesthetics is additive.

Lidocaine (lignocaine) plain 4.5 mg/kg (max 300 mg), with adrenaline 7 mg/kg (max 500 mg); bupivacaine about 2 mg/kg (max 150 to 175 mg depending on labelling); ropivacaine 3 mg/kg (max 200 mg); prilocaine 6 mg/kg (max 400 mg).
Use ultrasound guidance for peripheral blocks (reduces LAST risk by about 60%), aspirate before each injection, and inject in aliquots under 5 mL with pauses of 30 to 45 seconds.
Consider an adrenaline-containing test dose as an intravascular marker: heart rate rise of 10 beats/min or more, or systolic rise of 15 mmHg or more.
Stock a LAST kit with 20% lipid emulsion and the checklist wherever large-volume local anaesthetic is given, including labour wards, dental, dermatology and day-care theatres.

sections.title: Higher-risk patients
items: Reduce doses at the extremes of age (neonates, infants, elderly), and in cardiac failure, conduction disease, hepatic impairment and low muscle mass.
Pregnancy: greater sensitivity and faster absorption; treat LAST the same way with lipid, and follow maternal cardiac arrest steps (left uterine displacement, early delivery decision).
Children: use mg/kg limits strictly; the lipid dose is the same weight-based regimen (1.5 mL/kg bolus, 0.25 mL/kg/min).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Treating LAST cardiac arrest with standard 1 mg adrenaline doses, vasopressin or lidocaine.
Waiting for cardiac arrest before giving lipid emulsion.
Forgetting delayed toxicity during continuous catheter infusions or after truncal fascial plane blocks.
Adding doses of two local anaesthetics as if they were independent, or dosing obese patients on total body weight.

drugs.name: Lipid emulsion 20% (for example Intralipid)
drugs.dose: Over 70 kg: 100 mL IV over 2 to 3 min, then 200 to 250 mL over 15 to 20 min. Under 70 kg: 1.5 mL/kg over 2 to 3 min, then 0.25 mL/kg/min
drugs.notes: If unstable repeat bolus and double infusion; continue at least 15 minutes after stability; maximum about 12 mL/kg. UK (AAGBI) regimen is similar: 1.5 mL/kg over 1 minute then 15 mL/kg/h.

drugs.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine)
drugs.dose: 1 mcg/kg IV or less per bolus in LAST arrest or hypotension
drugs.notes: Avoid standard 1 mg doses; avoid vasopressin.

drugs.name: Lorazepam
drugs.dose: 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg), may repeat once after 5 to 10 minutes
drugs.notes: Midazolam in small IV increments is an alternative; benzodiazepines are preferred for LAST seizures.

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.dose: 300 mg IV bolus for shock-refractory VF or pulseless VT (adult ALS dosing)
drugs.notes: Preferred antiarrhythmic; do not use lidocaine.

drugs.name: Lidocaine (lignocaine) maximum dose
drugs.dose: Plain 4.5 mg/kg (max 300 mg); with adrenaline 7 mg/kg (max 500 mg)

drugs.name: Bupivacaine maximum dose
drugs.dose: About 2 mg/kg (max 150 mg per UK labelling, 175 mg in some references)
drugs.notes: Most cardiotoxic; resuscitation can be prolonged.
